questions.story: 2:45 PM — An attacker has logged into your Instagram/Facebook business account, changed recovery details, and sent scam links to your customers.
questions.question: What is your critical containment response?
options: Pay the WhatsApp scammer who offered to recover the account for a fee.
Use the official "Forgot Password" or account recovery workflow on the social media platform to remove unknown access and secure the account.
Create a brand-new page immediately and abandon the old one.
Reply to the customers' messages telling them to click the link anyway.
questions.feedback: Official account-recovery channels provide the appropriate way to regain control and remove unauthorized access. Paying an attacker or unverified third party can create additional risk.

questions.story: 2:55 PM — Customers have already received malicious links from your hijacked business profile.
questions.question: How should you handle customer communication during this incident?
options: Keep quiet and hope no one clicks the links.

Post a warning through trusted secondary channels, such as WhatsApp Status, another verified business channel, or the business website, informing customers that the main account was compromised and advising them not to click recent links.
Blame the platform publicly for bad security.
Block all customers who received the message.
questions.feedback: Proactive communication can reduce the risk of customers interacting with the malicious links and helps clarify which communications from the compromised account should not be trusted.

questions.story: 3:30 PM — You have successfully regained access to the business account through the official recovery process.
questions.question: Which recovery checklist provides the strongest protection against another takeover?
options: Update the password to a strong phrase, enable 2FA using an authenticator app, review linked third-party apps, and remove unfamiliar recovery emails/numbers.
Change the profile picture and username.
Delete all customer chats and turn off direct messaging.
Save your password in a public Google Doc for your team.
questions.feedback: Strengthening authentication, reviewing connected applications, and removing unfamiliar recovery options reduces the risk of the attacker retaining or regaining access.

questions.story: 3:45 PM — You have regained control of the business account and removed unfamiliar recovery details.
questions.question: What should you verify before considering the account fully recovered?
options: Confirm that only authorized users and devices have access, review recent account activity, and document the recovery actions taken.
Immediately give the new password to customers so they can verify the account.
Delete all previous messages and login notifications.
Turn off 2FA so employees can access the account more easily.
questions.feedback: Confirming authorized access and reviewing recent activity helps identify any remaining unauthorized access or suspicious activity. Documenting the recovery actions also preserves an incident record.
